PullRequest.Title: Add custom agent skill suggestions

## Summary

Adds provider-backed `skills` value support for GitHub Copilot custom agent files:

- completes enabled, disabled, and temporarily unavailable skills from every matching harness inventory
- shows skill descriptions, source, load status, and availability in completions and hovers
- marks authoritative unknown, disabled, and unavailable skill references as unnecessary
- remains fail-open while any matching inventory is pending or failed
- reuses `provideChatSessionCustomizations` and its existing change event instead of adding a new provider API

Part of #342881.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\promptSyntax\languageProviders\promptHeaderAutocompletion.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\promptSyntax\languageProviders\promptHovers.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\promptSyntax\languageProviders\promptValidator.test.ts` — 304 tests passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run eslint -- <7 changed TypeScript files>` — passed
- `npx component-explorer render -p .\test\componentFixtures\component-explorer.json --workers 4 --timeout 30000` — 4,330 fixtures rendered without errors

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The diff-introduced direct call, editor validation frequency, IPC forwarding, full-array serialization, provider cache contract, and existing cached consumer pattern are all explicit in repository code. Exact provider latency and users' inventory sizes vary, which affects magnitude but not the repeated boundary mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: extension-host IPC calls, provider-side inventory discovery, full customization-array serialization, and per-call filtering/allocation
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For each validation, completion, or skill hover, the cost is one full inventory request per matching harness; validation is triggered after every 200 ms editing pause for each open agent model, and provider-change validation fans out across all open models. When no matching harness is active, all matching harnesses are queried concurrently.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: repeated IPC and inventory work, increased extension-host CPU/I/O, and delayed diagnostics/completion/hover responses while the full inventories are rebuilt and serialized
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, skill language features did not invoke provideChatSessionCustomizations. Existing customization UI consumers cache each provider result and invalidate it only from itemProvider.onDidChange, matching the proposed API lifecycle contract.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new resolver directly invokes provideChatSessionCustomizations for every matching descriptor each time resolveAgentFileSkills is called. The new validator calls it on every debounced edit of an agent file with a skills attribute, while completion and hover call it again independently.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 39 directly calls itemProvider.provideChatSessionCustomizations inside resolveAgentFileSkills; all three newly added language-feature paths call this resolver, and no cache or in-flight coalescing exists in the new file.
Findings.Title: Cache the customization inventory instead of re-querying providers
Findings.Impact: Editing a GitHub Copilot agent that has `skills` now causes every 200 ms validation pause to fetch and serialize the complete customization inventory (agents, skills, instructions, hooks, prompts—not just skills) from each matching harness. Extension-backed harnesses cross the main-thread/ext-host boundary, and built-in providers perform collection-wide discovery; diagnostics wait for these calls, with additional calls on completion and hover.
Findings.Evidence: promptFileContributions.ts ModelTracker validates 200 ms after each content change and validateAll revalidates every open prompt model on provider events. The added validateCopilotSkills path reaches this line with CancellationToken.None. MainThreadChatAgents2 forwards provideChatSessionCustomizations to ExtHostChatAgents2 over IPC, where the entire returned item array is mapped and serialized. The API documentation states the UI calls this provider once, caches the result, and re-queries only after onDidChange; ItemProviderItemSource/PureItemProviderItemSource implement exactly that cache. PromptsServiceCustomizationItemProvider also shows that a call resolves all five customization types and performs collection-wide discovery before this resolver filters for skills.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache/coalesce the inventory per descriptor and session resource, return filtered skills from that cache, and invalidate it from itemProvider.onDidChange (and descriptor/session changes). Share that cache across validation, completion, and hover rather than calling the provider directly on each request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editing an open GitHub Copilot custom-agent file that contains a skills sequence
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After each content change, ModelTracker's 200 ms delayer invokes PromptValidator.validate; validateCopilotAgent awaits validateCopilotSkills, which awaits all matching harness inventories before markers are committed. If a tools sequence is also present, tool resolution completes first, then the newly added skill inventory request runs serially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call extension-contributed provideChatSessionCustomizations and serialize/map the complete returned customization array across main-thread/ext-host RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC round trip per extension-backed matching harness per validation; H requests run concurrently, and provider events can produce O(H × open matching agent files) requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Skill validation did not query customization providers; existing management consumers queried once and reused a cached result until onDidChange.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Diagnostics for the model are not committed until every matching inventory promise settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider-side collection-wide customization discovery, including agent/skill/prompt/instruction/hook inventory and agent-host plugin-content/built-in-skill enumeration where applicable
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reached once per in-process matching harness per validation; internal sub-results may be cached, but the provider still traverses and allocates the complete inventory before the resolver keeps only skills.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This discovery was not reached from skill validation and UI item sources cached its result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All provider discovery awaited by Promise.all is on the diagnostics critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One full provider request per matching harness for each validation of each open agent model containing skills. Normal typing is coalesced only within the 200 ms delay; provider-change events call validateAll for every open prompt model, and running validations use CancellationToken.None.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one skill resolution, Promise.all starts all matching harness requests concurrently with no shared limiter. Separate open-model validations and a new validation started after an earlier one has begun are not coalesced by the new resolver.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new resolver has no positive, negative, or in-flight cache. It ignores the provider's onDidChange-based cache lifecycle and requests the full inventory again on every validation. Existing customization item sources cache by session/provider and invalidate on onDidChange, demonstrating the intended warm-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the direct provider call, 200 ms validation trigger, all-harness Promise.all fan-out, CancellationToken.None, IPC forwarding, and API cache contract are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on installed matching harnesses, provider implementation, inventory size, and internal filesystem caches; the per-edit uncached boundary and complete-array serialization are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: repeated full-inventory provider calls and IPC were introduced on a typing-driven validation path without the cache/coalescing required by the provider lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Requesting completion inside a GitHub Copilot agent's skills sequence
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The completion provider awaits resolveAgentFileSkills and Promise.all over all matching inventories before it can build and return suggestions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and serialize complete customization inventories from extension-host providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: H IPC calls per completion request, where H is the effective number of matching harnesses after active-harness selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No provider boundary existed for skills completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The suggestion list is blocked on the slowest matching provider because Promise.all must settle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One complete inventory fetch per matching harness per completion invocation, with allocation proportional to the total customization inventory and then the number of skills/names.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All matching harnesses are queried concurrently for one request. Editor cancellation is forwarded, but there is no sharing with validation, hover, or another completion request and providers may already have performed work before cancellation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold and warm requests behave the same in the new resolver: every completion re-queries providers. There is no in-flight coalescing or event-invalidated cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new completion hunk directly calls the resolver and awaits its result.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Completion invocation frequency and provider latency vary, but one uncached full-inventory call per matching harness is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported shared-cache finding; the same introduced repeated boundary delays completion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hovering a referenced skill in a GitHub Copilot agent header
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hover resolution checks the skill under the pointer and then awaits resolveAgentFileSkills before constructing hover content.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and serialize complete provider customization arrays to resolve one hovered skill
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: H IPC calls per hover request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Skills hovers returned static attribute information and did not cross a provider boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Hover display waits for all matching harness inventory requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One complete inventory request per matching harness for each skill hover request; post-fetch matching scans the returned skill array.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Matching harness requests run concurrently within Promise.all. The editor token can cancel cooperative providers, but no result is shared with validation/completion or later hovers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No warm-cache path exists in the new resolver; repeated hovers re-query unchanged inventories despite onDidChange being available for invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed getSkillHover path directly awaits the resolver only when the pointer is over a scalar skill.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hover frequency is lower than validation frequency, so this is supporting impact rather than a separate finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding because it shares the same root cause and bounded cache fix as validation/completion.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. One high-confidence medium-severity regression was submitted: uncached full customization inventory requests are now repeated across typing-driven validation, completion, and hover, fanning out to every matching harness and crossing extension-host IPC where applicable. No concrete performance regression was found in the local skill matching/detail helpers or tests, and the PR does not itself establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
